title: location-lock-deprecation-and-graceful-customer-transition-notes
content:
Overview:

This doc captures working notes for deprecating the legacy "location-lock" model (old internal term) and moving affected Private/Dedicated customers to the new regional anchoring framework. The goal is a predictable, auditable, low-friction migration path that preserves contractual residency guarantees where required and minimizes operational lift for both customers and oncall.

Why deprecate location-lock? Short bullets:
- The legacy mechanism is brittle: ad-hoc routing hooks + tenant-specific overrides make audits and rollbacks hard.
- New regional anchoring (RA) provides: explicit evidence bundles, clear fallback hierarchy, and unified telemetry.
- Continued maintenance of location-lock increases risk of drift and security surface area.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Customer impact analysis (who/where/contractual obligations)
- Migration sequencing and timed deprecation windows
- Operator runbook for migrations and emergency rollback
- Customer communications (templates + schedule)
- Telemetry & acceptance criteria to mark a migration as complete
- Open questions and escalation paths

Non-scope: changes to hosted API behavior or Dedicated capacity autoscaling policies not related to routing/locality.

Customer impact snapshot (quick table in prose):
- High-risk customers (must remain within country): 6 tenants — need legal sign-off and manual migration windows
- Medium-risk (EU-only but flexible on region): ~14 tenants — can be moved in a staged, automated manner with preflight checks
- Low-risk: all remaining tenants; automated cutover safe after a short validation period

Principles that drive the plan:
- Minimize simultaneous migrations for high-risk tenants (one-per-week for manual migrations)
- Always produce an auditable artifact (evidence bundle) that ties customer ID -> region -> routing policy -> operator approval
- Keep a 48-hour rollback window after cutover for critical customers with human-in-the-loop rollback gating

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0–2: Finalize legal checklist and evidence bundle template (owners: Priya Shah + Legal)
- Week 2–4: Preflight scans across current location-lock assignments; generate customer impact reports (owner: Diego)
- Week 4–8: Pilot migrations for 3 low-risk tenants + internal canary (owner: Marina)
- Week 8–16: Staged migrations for medium-risk tenants, weekly cadence, automated rollback tests each night (owner: Liam)
- Week 16–24: Manual windows for high-risk tenants, coordinate with Sales and CSMs for contract amendments if needed (owner: Sofia)
- Week 24: Sunset location-lock feature toggle in control plane (condition: all evidence bundles generated and verified)

Migration mechanics (operator-friendly checklist):
1) Preflight (automated):
   - Run "ra-preflight --tenant <id>" to detect incompatible route rules (JIRA: PD-4723 preflight job)
   - Verify no active pin-override flags on tenant config
   - Generate evidence bundle: region map, last 30d access logs, existing S3/GCS bucket locations (artifact stored in S3 path: s3://rbw-evidence/<tenant>/preflight-<ts>.zip)
2) Customer notification: send templated migration notice (see templates below) and capture acceptance (email reply or signed acknowledgement)
3) Scheduling: pick a 2h maintenance window for low/medium risk; 4h for high-risk with legal present
4) Execution: run cutover script (ops/ra-cutover) in dry-run mode first; then execute live and watch telemetry dashboards
5) Validation: run sample traffic, check evidence bundle is produced, confirm routing table reflects RA policies, verify token latency within SLO
6) Post-cutover hold: 48h for high-risk, 24h medium, 6h low; during hold monitored by oncall with escalation matrix

Rollback plan (fast path):
- If severe error: trigger instant fallback to previous routing policy using rollback token (ops/ra-rollback --tenant <id> --token <token-id>). This restores previous region binding and invalidates the RA evidence bundle for that attempt.
- For partial failures (degraded latency only): enable traffic split 80/20 back to old routing for 2 hours and run root cause collect (collector: /ops/collect-rc)
- All rollbacks must be recorded in the audit log and reconcile report produced within 24h

Operator playbook (oncall checklist):
- Pre-shift: ensure latest RA tooling image is pulled and test harness green (command: ops/healthcheck)
- During migration: live monitor metrics: routing-mismatch-rate, 95th latency, token-cost-bps, region-failover-count
- Post-migration: run evidence verification job (ops/verify-evidence) and attach to JIRA ticket
- Escalation: if legal/regulatory doubt arises, immediately pause migration and page Legal + Compliance channel with ticket link

Customer communications (templates & cadence):
- Initial notice (30 days before migration): short description, reasons, what changes (no data movement outside stated region), proposed window, CSM contact
- Reminder (7 days before): include rollback policy, expected downtime (0 mins for most), forced maintenance window if acceptance not received
- Day-of escalation message: minute-by-minute updates to CSM + customer primary contact via email and Slack
- Post-migration report (within 24h): evidence bundle link, telemetry summary, rollback token id if any fallback exercised

Example email subject/body (short, usable):
Subject: Upcoming change to location handling for your Redwood deployment — action required
Body: Hi <Name>, we plan to move your deployment to Redwood's regional anchoring (RA) on <date>. This aligns with your residency requirements. Expected impact: none for steady-state traffic; short maintenance window (<2h) for verification. Please reply to confirm or raise concerns by <date>.

Telemetry & acceptance criteria (automated checks):
- Evidence bundle creation success = 100% for migrated tenants
- Routing-match-rate >= 99.95% in validation window
- 95th percentile latency delta <= +15% vs baseline
- No unauthorized cross-region access events in last 30d post-cutover
- Alert if token-cost-bps increases > 30% for a sustained 1h window (requires signoff to keep change)

Audit artifacts to retain:
- Evidence bundle (signed by operator)
- Migration ticket with timestamps and logs
- Rollback tokens and decisions
- Customer acknowledgement (email or signed doc)

Open questions & unresolved items:
- Legal needs to confirm whether evidence bundle format is acceptable for DE and UK regulators (PRIORITY) — owner: Priya
- Do we need a dedicated HSM export of key origin for high-risk customers? (security input required) — owner: Security team (requested)
- Pricing impact for manual migrations (CS asks for guidance on cost credits/refunds) — owner: Finance/CS
- Automation gap: no current UI for scheduling staged migrations; backlog item GH-2147 (owner: DevEx)

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Priya: finalize evidence bundle template and run one mock with Legal (due: 2024-11-20)
- Diego: run preflight scan across all tenants and produce CSV of risk categories (due: 2024-11-13)
- Marina: prepare pilot runbook and internal canary checklist (due: 2024-11-18)
- Liam: wire up a temporary dashboard panel with routing-match-rate and latency deltas for pilots (due: 2024-11-15)

Notes to self / rough thoughts (informal):
- Might be worth offering a "migration concierge" (paid) for large enterprise customers — reduces friction and gives us better control over schedule
- Consider small A/B of telemetry thresholds to tune rollback sensitivity (avoid false positives)
- Need to add a Preflight 'why-blocked' human-readable field in scan output so CSMs can explain issues to customers

References & pointers:
- Confluence: Location Lock Migration Plan (linked above)
- JIRA PD-4723 (preflight scans), PD-5238 (operator runbook)
- Slack: #private-deployments and thread ts:1678423200.000200

If you're reviewing: add comments inline or ping me in Slack. This is a working doc — expect iterations.
